source.title: Scaling Relationship on Learning Mathematical Reasoning with Large Language Models
source.authors: Zheng Yuan; Hongyi Yuan; Cheng Li; Guanting Dong; Ke-Ming Lu; Chuan-Qi Tan; Chang Zhou; Jing-Ren Zhou

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether downstream mathematical-reasoning accuracy is associated with pre-training loss or model scale, using GSM8K accuracy rather than held-out pre-training loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own GSM8K SFT accuracies across model sizes and discusses their relationship to pre-training loss. ICL and GPT-3 results in the discussion are taken from cited work, not counted as this study's results. The supervised-data-amount and rejection-sampling experiments vary different factors and do not test the listed power-law, compute-allocation, or downstream scale/pre-training-loss versions.
record.test_reason: The authors fine-tune LLaMA and LLaMA2 (7B–70B) on GSM8K themselves. They relate the SFT accuracies to model scale and to reported pre-training loss, which bears on V6 (downstream predictability). No version about pre-training loss scaling (V1–V5, V7) is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the following: SFT accuracy is log-linear in supervised data amount; better (lower-loss) models benefit less from SFT and RFT; RFT gains track distinct reasoning paths. The authors' headline is that lowering pre-training loss matters most for math reasoning.
record.recipe_differences: Measures GSM8K downstream accuracy after SFT and compares it with model scale and reported pre-training loss; it does not fit held-out language-model loss power laws or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that pre-training losses correspond to different datasets and tokenizers and cannot be strictly compared; they also limit the approximate linear loss-accuracy relation to the interval shown.

fits_no_version.finding: GSM8K SFT accuracy is log-linear in the amount of supervised data over 1/8 to 1 of the training set. Larger, lower-loss models gain less per doubling (Table 5, Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream fine-tuning accuracy scales log-linearly with fine-tuning data, with returns shrinking for stronger base models.

fits_no_version.finding: RFT gains shrink as sampling count k doubles, tracking the number of distinct reasoning paths (Table 2, Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains from self-generated augmentation scale with distinct-path count and show diminishing returns.

record.problems: The paper says losses across the compared models are not strictly comparable because they come from different pre-training datasets and tokenizers. It does not regress scaling laws, and the described loss-accuracy relationship is only approximate and limited to the observed interval. The tabled downstream accuracies do not include uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the included GSM8K SFT scale results. Cited ICL and GPT-3 results were not included as study results; the supervised-data-amount and rejection-sampling experiments vary different factors from the claim versions.

untested.parts: Tasks other than GSM8K. Settings other than SFT and greedy decoding as the authors' own runs (ICL numbers are cited). No fitted predictive law or extrapolation test.
Not tested: no held-out pre-training loss vs N/D/C.
Not tested as a power law. The fine-tuning data scaling reported is log-linear accuracy, not loss (see fits_no_version).

missing.what: Pre-training loss values paired with SFT accuracy (1.8, 1.75, 1.73, 1.68, 1.62) for the five models, which form the loss–accuracy relation
RFT-U13B/U33B accuracies across sizes, showing gaps between same-size models narrowing (e.g. 7B 49.3 vs 7B-2 50.3)
SFT accuracy by model under downsampled data. The scale ordering breaks at low data (e.g. 13B at 1/32 data, 3 epochs: 0.0)

record.verdict_notes: The ICL and GPT-3 points in Fig. 2 are cited results, not the study's own. The rows are single accuracies, so the V6 trend appears only across rows r1–r7. 65B and 70B lack stated pre-training losses.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pre-training loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating pre-training losses from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations and their trends with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes.
Only GSM8K mathematical reasoning after SFT is measured here; general downstream tasks and a general predictive law are not tested.
The study notes that its pre-training losses and setups are not aligned and does not regress scaling laws; it does not test how fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits vary with fitting choices.

relationships.condition: LLaMA/LLaMA2 7B–70B, full GSM8K SFT, greedy decoding
relationships.reason: SFT accuracy rises monotonically, from 35.9 to 63.2, as pre-training loss falls (1.8→1.62) and as size grows (r1–r7). The authors call the loss–accuracy relation approximately linear.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased monotonically from 35.9 to 63.2 as pretraining loss decreased from 1.8 to 1.62 and size increased, with an approximately linear loss–accuracy relationship.

relationships.condition: Loss–accuracy relation across model families with differing tokenizers and data
relationships.reason: The authors say the linear relation holds only within the observed loss interval. The losses are not strictly comparable, and no law was regressed. So predictability is qualitative here (r1–r7, Sec. 3.1 and Limitations).
relationships.display_finding: The linear loss–accuracy relationship held only within the observed interval, with losses not strictly comparable across families and predictability remaining qualitative.

relationships.reason: Per the text (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 5, Table 5), augmented data shrinks the accuracy gaps between equal-size models. The authors suggest model size, not pre-training loss, then becomes the indicator. The indicator of downstream scaling thus depends on the amount of fine-tuning data. No row records this.
relationships.display_finding: Augmented fine-tuning data narrowed accuracy gaps between equal-size models, leading the authors to suggest model size became the more useful indicator.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
